headline: Underground Forum Dedicated to Gas Station Bathroom Reviews Hits 50,000 Members
subheadline: r/PorcelainPitstops celebrates milestone with controversial 'Golden Toilet' awards
summary: A Threadit community dedicated to rating gas station restrooms has grown from niche hobby to cultural phenomenon.
content:
What started as a joke between truckers has become one of Threadit's most dedicated communities: r/PorcelainPitstops, a forum exclusively devoted to reviewing gas station bathrooms across the country.

The subreddit, which celebrated its 50,000th member this week, operates with the rigor of a Michelin guide. Reviewers rate facilities on a 5-star scale across categories including "Soap Quality," "Graffiti Creativity," "Floor Wetness (Mysterious)," and "Likelihood of Paranormal Encounter."

"People think we're joking," said moderator u/ToiletTrekker, who claims to have reviewed 847 gas station bathrooms since 2019. "We're not joking. This is important work."

The community's annual "Golden Toilet" awards, announced last weekend, sparked heated debate. The Shell station on Highway 47 took top honors, praised for its "surprisingly aggressive hand dryer" and "graffiti that asked genuine philosophical questions."

Controversy erupted when a Flying J in Nebraska received the "Brown Toilet" award for worst bathroom. Supporters of the establishment have launched a counter-campaign, claiming the review was conducted during "unrepresentative circumstances."

"There was a raccoon in there that day," explained a Flying J representative. "That's not typical."

The community has also developed its own terminology. A bathroom with good lighting but poor ventilation is called a "Flashbang." One that's clean but somehow still feels wrong is a "Uncanny Lavatory." A perfect bathroom is simply called "The Myth."

"I've been searching for The Myth my whole life," u/ToiletTrekker said. "I'll know it when I see it."

The subreddit's most upvoted post of all time is simply a photo of a bathroom that had two toilets facing each other, titled "For when you need emotional support."
author: Chris Patterson, Human Interest
